correctness.rationale: The renewal recursion gives u1/u2/u3 exactly, and for n>=4 u_n is a convex combination of four previous masses, including u0=1, proving the global minimum reduces to min(u1,u2,u3), including periodic/vanishing-probability cases. Algebraic deficits are u1−P4=a[c+d(1+a−b)], u2−P4=b²+bc+d[a²+b(1−a)], u3−P4=ab(b+c)+c(1−a²): all nonnegative on the entire closed simplex. Change variables to cumulative s1=a,s2=a+b,s3=a+b+c; P4=s1s2s3+2s1(s2−s1)(1−s3), whose terminal specializations have degrees 1,2,3. Taking a=b=t,c=0,d=1−2t gives u3−(Q4+alpha abd)=t²[(2−alpha)+(2alpha−3)t], negative for sufficiently small t if alpha>2, establishing exact sharpness of this restricted direction.

originality.rationale: The complete Nikolov–Savov original article, Conjecture 3.7, expressly asserts Q_k maximal in A_k and largest in restricted hat A_k for each k>=3, and Proposition 3.8 proves only k=3. Their Theorem 3.6 proves absence of a largest element in the unrestricted class, which does not imply failure of maximality of a given Q4 or restriction to hat A4. This explicit dominating P4, cumulative-class membership and coefficient-optimal direction are not in the inspected original and no equivalent later result was found in targeted published SCOPE/Resultary comparisons. Later unindexed disproof remains historical risk.
